newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan MOF says may seek more funds for Nissan Life.
newsitem.headline: Japan MOF says may seek more funds for Nissan Life.

text.p: A senior official of the Ministry of Finance said on Tuesday that it may ask life insurers to allow for more money to be given from an industry fund to a new firm to be set up to take over the policies of failed insurer Nissan Mutual Life Co.
"If the losses (of Nissan Life), should exceed 200 billion yen, we may ask for an increase in the amount," said Makoto Fukuda, the director of the ministry's insurance department.
The insurance industry is currently drawing up a scheme for Nissan Life, the first life insurance firm to fail in Japan's post-war history.
The Policyholders Protection Fund, to which 44 life insurers contribute, can presently inject up to 200 billion yen into a company that would take over the policies of a failed insurer.
Fukuda said this amount could be increased if the rules were changed.

He also added that it was possible under present laws to change the high returns Nissan Life guaranteed on its individual pension policies if the policies were to be taken over by another firm as part of the scheme.

Industry sources say that nearly half of Nissan Life's assets are individual pension policies guaranteeing an annual return of 5.5 percent. The high returns damaged the firm's financial stability and were key factor in its failure.
Fukuda said he hoped that the industry would come up with a scheme all relevant parties would agree to, referring to Hitachi Ltd and Nissan Motor Co Ltd, Nissan Life's two biggest clients.
He added that the two firms also had personnel ties with the life insurer as some of their officials held positions as outside directors at Nissan Life.
